cim: Governor Hochul Breaks Ground on Permanent Empire AI Supercomputing Center, Marking Major Milestone in New York’s National Leadership in Using Artificial Intelligence for the Public Good
cim_eredeti: Governor Hochul Breaks Ground on Permanent Empire AI Supercomputing Center, Marking Major Milestone in New York’s National Leadership in Using Artificial Intelligence for the Public Good
szoveg_eredeti:
Groundbreaking at University at Buffalo Marks Next Chapter of Governor’s Historic Empire AI Initiative, Building on Successful Launch of Nation’s Most Powerful Academic AI Research Computer

State-of-the-Art Facility Will Expand World-Class Computing Power for New York Researchers While Setting New Standards for Energy Efficiency and Environmental Responsibility

Milestone Complements on New York’s Nation-Leading RAISE Act on Frontier AI Accountability and Launch of Center for AI Responsibility and Research at Binghamton University to Advance Independent Research Into AI Safety and Security

Governor Kathy Hochul today officially broke ground on the permanent home of Empire AI at the University at Buffalo, marking a major milestone in New York’s historic effort to lead artificial intelligence research for the public good. The groundbreaking launches the next phase of development for Empire AI Gamma, the full-scale supercomputing facility that will dramatically expand the computing power available to researchers at New York’s leading public and private universities and establishing Empire AI as the most powerful academic AI research computer in the country. First announced by Governor Hochul in her 2024 State of the State address, Empire AI has grown into a more than $500 million public-private initiative that is already supporting groundbreaking research in medicine, climate science, advanced manufacturing and other fields, while establishing New York as a national model for responsible AI innovation.

Today’s groundbreaking comes just days after Governor Hochul launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at Binghamton University, a first-of-its-kind research initiative bringing together more than 80 scientists to independently study the safety, security and performance of advanced AI systems using Empire AI’s computing infrastructure. Together, these investments are advancing the Governor’s vision of a statewide AI research ecosystem that gives academic researchers the tools, infrastructure and expertise needed to accelerate scientific discovery and ensure artificial intelligence serves the public good.

“Two years ago, we made a commitment to put New York at the forefront of the AI revolution — while ensuring safe and responsible AI development is a top priority — and today we are delivering on that promise,” Governor Hochul said. “Empire AI is already giving our brightest researchers the most powerful academic AI computing resources in the country, and now we’re building the permanent home that will take this initiative to an entirely new level. From advancing medical breakthroughs to tackling climate change, we’re proving that New York can lead the nation in artificial intelligence while building responsibly, creating opportunities and making sure this technology benefits all New Yorkers.”

Building the Future of AI Research in New York

This new permanent facility represents the next chapter of the historic buildout of Empire AI. Expected to be completed by early 2028, Empire AI Gamma will provide the infrastructure needed to dramatically expand computing capabilities and support increasingly ambitious research across New York’s leading academic institutions. Empire AI is already demonstrating the value of its approach. By bringing together New York’s leading academic institutions around a shared computing resource, Empire AI allows scientists to tackle bigger questions, accelerate research timelines and pursue discoveries that would otherwise be beyond the reach of individual universities.

Launched by Governor Hochul in April 2024, Empire AI is a first-in-the-nation consortium of leading public and private research institutions providing academic researchers with access to world-class AI computing power that no single university could afford independently. Just six months later, the Governor launched Empire AI Alpha, made possible by a philanthropic contribution from the Simons Foundation, giving hundreds of researchers immediate access to advanced computing resources. In August 2026, Empire AI Beta, a $40 million supercomputer, became fully operational at the University at Buffalo, delivering 11 times the AI training capacity, 40 times the inference performance and eight times the data storage of Alpha.

“Two years ago, we made a commitment to put New York at the forefront of the AI revolution — while ensuring safe and responsible AI development is a top priority — and today we are delivering on that promise.”

Empire AI Board Chair Tom Secunda said, “Just two years ago, Empire AI was an ambitious idea, and today it is a national model for putting world-class computing power in the hands of academic researchers, with more than 1,500 registered users and hundreds of research projects already underway. Thanks to Governor Hochul’s vision and leadership, New York has brought together government, universities and philanthropy to build a scientific resource that no single institution could create on its own. This groundbreaking takes that commitment to the next level, strengthening New York’s leadership and helping shape the future of scientific discovery across the nation.”

Co-founder and chair of the Simons Foundation Marilyn Simons said, “Many of the greatest scientific breakthroughs begin with a question no one has been able to answer. Empire AI gives more scientists the tools to tackle those questions. We are grateful to Governor Hochul for bringing together New York’s leading research institutions and philanthropic partners to make this extraordinary shared resource possible. Today’s groundbreaking is an investment in the next generation of scientists and in discoveries that will benefit us all.”

State University of New York Chancellor John B. King Jr. said, “Empire AI is driving New York State’s leadership in leveraging AI to achieve research excellence that advances the public good. From accelerating the search for cures and treatments for disease to enhancing speech language therapy for children, and from advancing biotechnology research to tackling climate change, SUNY researchers are addressing some of society’s most pressing challenges thanks to Empire AI. SUNY is proud to host Empire AI at the State University of New York at Buffalo, and we are grateful to Governor Hochul for her vision and steadfast leadership.”

The SUNY Board of Trustees said, “Visionary leadership from Governor Hochul makes it possible for SUNY and our higher education partners to pioneer research for the public good through Empire AI. The permanent Empire AI facility will accelerate groundbreaking research and innovations that improve communities throughout New York State and beyond.”

Empire State Development President, CEO & Commissioner Hope Knight said, “Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, New York is proving that when we invest in broad, responsible access to cutting-edge technology, our entire economy wins. Today’s groundbreaking at the University at Buffalo marks a major step forward for Empire AI — creating jobs now while empowering New York’s students, researchers, and businesses to drive innovation, attract new investment, and deliver lasting economic benefits to communities across the state.”

U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand said, “New York State is setting the national standard for responsible AI. Empire AI at the University at Buffalo represents a $500 million investment in our future, fueling cutting-edge research and proving that artificial intelligence can be harnessed safely as a powerful force for the public good.”

Congressmember Tim Kennedy said, “For decades, the world has looked to New York State to lead the way in technological advancement. With this historic groundbreaking at UB, we continue that tradition by advancing research that benefits New Yorkers in a secure and responsible manner.
